Nominations Committee of the Board The Nominations Committee advises the Board on matters concerning the membership of the Board and Board Committees. Remuneration Committee The Remuneration Committee is responsible for overseeing the pay, benefits and conditions of employment of the Vice-Chancellor and the other senior staff. Courses and programmes Applying from your country or region Fees and scholarships Student visas Student accommodation Contacts Twitter Facebook Instagram YouTube Weibo Staff intranet Guidance for agents This area is designed to help you advise and support your students, and to manage applications to the University of Bristol on behalf of international applicants. Jump to section Postgraduate applications Undergraduate applications Our commitment We value our partnerships with our international agents and the support they give to their students. The University of Bristol is committed to the UK Agent Quality Framework (AQF) and pledge to create and maintain the highest standards of agent management, ensuring the UK remains a leading study destination for international students. We continue to work to ensure that the relationships between recruitment partners, applicants and the University remain fair and transparent. We have signed the pledge to ensure our standards are in-line with the Good practice guide for education agents and the National Code of Ethical Practice for UK Education Agents , as published by the British Council. We encourage all our agent representatives to circulate the Study UK guide to choosing an education agent to students seeking their services. Postgraduate applications Agent Portal Agents and agencies use the Agent Portal to create, submit and manage postgraduate applications to the University of Bristol on behalf of international applicants. Sign in to the Agent Portal Help with managing applications Read the guidance document on how to use the Agent Portal. Agent Portal guidance (Office document, 48kB) Agent Portal guidance (PDF, 138kB) This includes information about how to: Sign in to the Agent Portal Manage and submit applications Withdraw an application. Help with managing agent profiles Agency managers have the role of 'super users' in the Agent Portal. Super users can: Create, edit and deactivate agent accounts View linked applications View agency details. Guidance Agent Portal guidance for super users (Office document, 36kB) Agent Portal guidance for super users (PDF, 91kB) Agent authorisation form This form is to be completed by applicants to postgraduate programmes who wish to use the services of an official University of Bristol agent. It also includes our data protection statement. Agent authorisation form (Office document, 100kB) Agent authorisation form (PDF, 522kB) Undergraduate applications Linking undergraduate applications Agents may need to complete a tagging form to inform us of undergraduate applicants they are supporting to apply to the University of Bristol. The form will link the agent with a submitted application. If the applicant has used the agent's UCAS Apply Centre, the application will be automatically linked and you do not need to complete the form. The form must be completed if: The applicant has applied directly The applicant has not used the agent's UCAS Apply Centre. Link an undergraduate application Contact us If you have any issues with the agent portal or require further information, contact international-office@bristol.ac.uk . Would you like to arrange a wellbeing session for you and colleagues? From yoga to reiki, massage to mental health awareness workshops, why not check out the facilitators directory to see what’s available. Looking after yourself The health and happiness of our staff is of paramount importance to us. We are committed to providing support where we can, to help you deal with any issues around your mental health and wellbeing. Time to Change In 2017 we signed the 'Time to Change' pledge, and we offer a range of programmes and services to support staff wellbeing. If you are experiencing a life threatening emergency, please call 999 now. If you feel that your mental health is at breaking point, you can speak to the Bristol Mental Health Crisis Team . Use the resources we've listed here to help look after yourself and your colleagues. If you have feedback on any of the Staff Health and Wellbeing initiatives or programmes you have experienced, please email staff-wellbeing-enquiries@bristol.ac.uk . We spend a large proportion of our lives at work, and it’s important to create a healthy working environment where wellbeing is integrated into everything we do. Providing a safe and healthy working environment allows staff to feel supported and empowers us all to achieve our best. We are proud of the diverse workforce that we have and recognise that everyone approaches their mental health and wellbeing differently. We want to continue to break down the barriers and encourage all our community to seek support and help when needed. Please explore the resources on the Wellbeing SharePoint site and if you have any suggestions or feedback, email staff-wellbeing-enquiries@bristol.ac.uk . James Bigwood, Chief People Officer As staff, I believe we have the right to a healthy and supportive environment, especially in regard to our mental health. I recognise the stresses and difficulties individuals can face both inside and outside the workplace, and I am here to facilitate discussion, understanding and support where necessary. I am well-versed in a variety of techniques and materials, and I am confident that we can work together to find the appropriate support to enable you to overcome challenges and move forward.
